newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 4.29 pct in strong recovery.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 4.29 pct in strong recovery.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted strong gains on Thursday in a continued recovery further buoyed by delayed payments ahead of a holiday, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed 64 points, or 4.29 percent higher at 1,556, recouping a total of 6.21 percent since Tuesday's 6.98 percent plunge caused by political worries and higher-than-expected January inflation.
Trade volume also jumped to 33.8 trillion lira ($288.3 million) from Wednesday's 26.6 trillion ($227.2 million).

Brokers said buying was encouraged by the holiday which caused payments of today's transactions to be delayed to next Wednesday and Friday's to next Thursday. Turkish markets will be closed next Monday and Tuesday due to a Moslem holiday.

"The recovery accelerated because yesterday's selective buys spilled over to most of the shares today. Political worries have eased and the market may again test the 1,700 barrier on Friday," said Murat Aktas from Yasar investment.
The index had lost 13.82 percent by Tuesday's close from the January 27 all-time high closing of 1,700 after a 74.2 percent surge from end-1996. It has regained 6.21 percent since Tuesday.
